newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Air Force agrees to safeguards for antelope.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Air Force agrees to safeguards for antelope.

text.p: A national wildlife group said Wednesday the Air Force has agreed to temporarily restrict military training in the region of Arizona's Sonoran Desert that is home to the endangered pronghorn antelope.
"This is a great step in the right direction for protecting one of our most endangered species," Rodger Schlickeisen, president of the Defenders of Wildlife, said in a statement.
That organisation sued the Air Force in September to force it to halt training in the antelopes' habitat.
A comment from Air Force was not immediately available.
The wildlife group said there may be fewer than 100 remaining of the antelope species that is judged the fastest land mammal in the Western Hemisphere.

The wildlife group said under the interim settlement, the Air Force will temporarily close one of two bomb training sites within the pronghorn's range. The other will be have new monitoring rules to reduce the pronghorns' risks of being bombed, it said.
The Air Force and the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service will continue to consult on longer-term plans to protect the antelope during military training.
